messages:
elaine: heads up — after the host runtime deploy this morning I'm seeing a 5-8% p99 tail increase on hosted requests. host CPU for tokenization/parse up noticeably. cc @chris @torey
chris: can you paste the flame/trace and a quick repro? is this only on HTTP/gRPC ingress or both?
elaine: quick snapshot from low-overhead host (canary) — flame points to `HostParse::tokenize` and `Ingress::proto_unwrap` spikes
elaine: perf top snippet:
```
HostParse::tokenize  34.2%
Ingress::proto_unwrap 18.7%
KVCache::lookup      9.6%
GRPCWriteV::flush     6.1%
```
elaine: link to trace: https://internal.perf/trace/686543 (internal)
torey: noticed kv cache hit-rate dropped around same window. rolling window shows hit% 87 -> 61 after selector change. could be kernel selection causing subtle seq-length padding -> different cache keys
chris: strange — kernel selector change should be orthogonal. did selector alter batching hints (prefer_small_batch_kernels) or change token-framing behavior?
elaine: deploy included a tiny heuristic tweak: prefer smaller kernel for short sequences to reduce kernel launch overhead. didn't think it would affect preparse path
torey: hypothesis: small-kernel path does additional framing on host (more copy/parse ops), causing extra host CPU before GPU. that increases request lat and evicts KV entries faster (work-stealing).
chris: +1. can we A/B the selector flag? toggle to old logic for a canary group and compare host parse time & kv hit rate?
dena: infra-bot: deploy v2.14.3 -> canary group started @6865429800 (10% hosts) :rocket:
elaine: ok running canary perf diff now. I also ran a microbench on tokenization with 100k short seqs. results:
```
before: tokenize 0.47us/op, memcopies 1.2MB/op
after:  tokenize 0.62us/op, memcopies 1.9MB/op
```
elaine: so small but at scale it explains the p99 shift and KV churn
torey: we should also add a lightweight metric: parse_bytes_copied and per-request kv_probe_count so we can correlate quickly next time
chris: agree. short-term revert the selector tweak in canary if diff matches production regression. long-term: make small-kernel path avoid extra framing by pushing framing into GPU-side unpack or reuse preparse buffer
elaine: can we try a hotfix: keep selector change but bypass host-framing when seq_len <= 64 (cheap path)?		

torey: that makes sense. simpler to ship than full revert. I'll prototype patch to skip extra copy on small seqs and add unit for kv key determinism
dena: infra-bot: created perf-ticket PERF-667 for tracking (assigned: @torey, @chris).
chris: i'll open two PRs: 1) add parse_bytes_copied + kv_probe_count to host telemetry, 2) kernel selector revert toggle + feature flag. will link PRs in PERF-667
elaine: rolling canary comparison shows host parse p99 back to baseline after toggling selector off on canary group; kv hit% recovered in ~5m window
chris: great. plan: ship selector flag off to remaining hosts while we land the copy-avoidance patch. notify ops channel before mass rollout.
torey: prototyping patch now, will push alpha by EOD. if tests pass I'll attach bench results
elaine: thanks — this one was subtle, good catch on KV correlation. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: note: follow-ups created -> PERF-667, PR#4891, PR#4892
